candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the victim's request URL and query parameters: GET /Delete.jsp?page=<page>&delete-all=1, GET /Rename.jsp?page=<page>&renameto=<name>, GET /Workflow.jsp?action=decide&id=<id>&outcome=outcome.decision.approve, GET /LostPassword.jsp?action=resetPassword&name=<email>. These need no token or body, so they can be embedded in an off-site page, e-mail or any renderable HTML.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified (a) the CsrfProtectionFilter ships in the war via jspwiki-http (jspwiki-main depends on it) and maps to /* in the web-fragment, but its checks are explicitly POST-only; (b) web.xml declares no security-constraint/http-method restriction for these JSPs (the only security-constraint block is commented out); (c) the affected JSPs still perform AuthorizationManager.hasAccess checks, so this is CSRF, not a broken access-control check; (d) the UI forms in templates/default/InfoContent.jsp and WorkflowContent.jsp use POST with CSRF tokens, so GET handling is not the intended flow; (e) sibling JSPs (DeleteGroup.jsp:54, EditGroup.jsp:57, NewGroup.jsp:61, Login.jsp:58, UserPreferences.jsp:69) contain the explicit isCsrfProtectedPost guard, showing the protection pattern was known and omitted here.
candidates.impact: An unauthenticated attacker can make a logged-in user delete or rename arbitrary wiki pages the victim is authorized to modify (data destruction, page hijacking), abort or approve pending workflow decisions (bypass of the approval control), and force password resets for accounts whose e-mail address is known (DoS/credential churn). Operations execute server-side with the victim's identity and are logged as the victim's actions.
candidates.prerequisites: Victim is logged in and authorized by the wiki policy for the action (delete/rename permission on the target page; default JSPWiki policies grant view/edit/comment/upload/delete/rename to the Authenticated role), or holds pending workflow decisions for Workflow.jsp. CSRF protection is POST-only, the affected JSPs have no method check, and web.xml security-constraints are commented out in this snapshot.
candidates.root_cause: CsrfProtectionFilter only inspects POST requests (doFilter checks isPost(); isCsrfProtectedPost() returns false for GET), and the per-JSP guards added in July 2022 (DeleteGroup.jsp:54, EditGroup.jsp:57, NewGroup.jsp:61, Login.jsp:58, UserPreferences.jsp:69) were not applied to the page-management and workflow handlers. Delete.jsp, Rename.jsp and Workflow.jsp therefore execute privileged state changes for plain GET requests containing only ordinary parameters, so a cross-site img/link/redirect can drive the victim's browser to perform them with the victim's session and permissions.
candidates.title: CSRF bypass: state-changing wiki operations execute on GET although CSRF protection only covers POST (page deletion, rename, workflow decisions, password reset)
candidates.trace: 1) CsrfProtectionFilter.doFilter (38-50) calls isPost() (65-67) and validates X-XSRF-TOKEN only for POST; requestContainsValidCsrfToken (61-63) is never reached for GET. 2) Delete.jsp builds a PAGE_DELETE context, checks only page authorization (44-45), reads delete-all from request parameters (55-56) and without any method/CSRF check calls PageManager.deletePage (69-82). 3) Rename.jsp reads renameto and calls PageRenamer.renamePage on GET (54, 70-84). 4) Workflow.jsp processes action=decide/action=abort directly from request parameters (56-101), even though templates/default/WorkflowContent.jsp (84-95) deliberately submits with method=POST plus wiki:CsrfProtection - the handler never enforces that intent. 5) LostPassword.jsp triggers a password reset when action=resetPassword is present (125-129), reachable by GET. Sibling guarded handlers show the intended pattern that is missing here.
candidates.unverified: The default WEB-INF/jspwiki.policy is absent from the snapshot, so the exact role-to-permission mapping (notably whether delete/rename are granted to Authenticated) could not be confirmed; a deployment restricting delete/rename to admins would expose only admin sessions. No code was executed and no request was sent, so nothing is runtime-confirmed. The snapshot contains no history/patch data, so it could not be confirmed whether a later upstream commit added the missing guard.
candidates.weakness_type: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CWE-352) / missing HTTP-method enforcement on state-changing endpoints

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot through the read-only tools: 1347 repository-root files, including jspwiki-main (auth, authz, attachment, content, filters, pages, parser, plugin, providers, render, search, tags, ui, ajax, workflow, xmlrpc), jspwiki-http (CsrfProtectionFilter, web-fragment), jspwiki-wysiwyg (htmltowiki), jspwiki-api, jspwiki-util, jspwiki-event, the Kendra/Tika search providers, the jspwiki-war JSP/template/script tree, servlet/filter configuration (web.xml, web-fragment.xml) and build files. Focused on attacker-controlled input paths, authorization/CSRF enforcement, JSP output escaping, file handling and XML/HTML parsing. Not every file was read line-by-line; JS bundles (mootools/prettify), CSS, translations and the portable/IT-test modules received only spot checks.
limitations: No unit/integration tests are present in the visible snapshot (no **/src/test/** files), so test-based confirmation of intended behavior was impossible.

WEB-INF/jspwiki.policy is not part of the snapshot; the exact default permission grants (e.g. delete/rename for Authenticated) could not be verified, though Installer/CoreResources confirm the policy file is expected at runtime.
No git history, patches, CVE/CWE labels, previous outputs or sibling cases were consulted; the snapshot is treated as the pre-fix state at 2.11.3-RC1 based only on pom.xml and ChangeLog.
No code was executed and no requests were sent; all conclusions are static-reading conclusions and are not runtime-confirmed.
The exact behavior of codelibs NekoHTML 2.0.2 regarding DOCTYPE/external entities could not be inspected, so the XXE lead remains unconfirmed rather than submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE/entity-expansion gap in jspwiki-wysiwyg HtmlStringToWikiTranslator (104-109): JDOM SAXBuilder over NekoHTML with ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA protections commented out, and untrusted htmlPageText reaches it from XHRHtml2Markup.jsp (view permission only) and Edit.jsp/Comment.jsp.
rejected_leads.reason: The protections are commented out (javax.xml.XMLConstants is not even imported) in three files, indicating long-standing upstream dead code rather than a regression; whether the codelibs NekoHTML 2.0.2 SAX driver resolves external general entities at all cannot be determined from the source snapshot. Unconfirmed hardening gap.

rejected_leads.lead: Open-redirect/redirect-validation bypass in AttachmentServlet.validateNextPage (353-363): only values containing '://' are blocked, so '//evil.example' passes.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only through the attacker's own CSRF-protected multipart upload POST (upload permission required), and in doGet 'nextpage' is URL-encoded before validation, so the redirect is self-inflicted with negligible impact.

rejected_leads.lead: JSON users AJAX endpoint (DefaultUserManager.JSONUserModule 428-477, registered with AllPermission at 109) returning a full UserProfile including the stored password hash for a caller-supplied uid.
rejected_leads.reason: The servlet is registered with AllPermission, so the dispatcher's validatePermission check is admin-only under a normal policy; a hardening issue rather than an externally exploitable vulnerability in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Unescaped EL output of group/member names in templates/default/GroupTab.jsp lines 141, 145, 149, 151, and raw scriptlet output in templates/210/GroupContent.jsp line 73.
rejected_leads.reason: DefaultGroupManager.validateGroup/checkGroupName validate the group name with InputValidator STANDARD (UNSAFE_PATTERN rejects <, >, quotes, &, ;) and member names with InputValidator.ID, so stored values cannot carry the needed HTML metacharacters in the normal save path.

The plugin is not declared in the module descriptors and is only registered as an AJAX servlet if first instantiated as a page plugin (edit rights required); response content type is also unset. Too speculative and low impact.

rejected_leads.lead: GET-triggered side effects in Logout.jsp/Captcha.jsp and possible header injection via attachment filenames in AttachmentServlet Content-Disposition (line 225).
rejected_leads.reason: Logout/Captcha side effects are minor and session-specific; modern containers reject CR/LF in header values, and AttachmentManager.validateFileName (286-314) splits/trims and replaces problematic filename characters.

summary: Apache JSPWiki 2.11.3-RC1 snapshot (~2022-07-30; 1347 visible files: Java, JSP, JS, resources; unit/integration tests and WEB-INF/jspwiki.policy are absent). I reviewed the filter/servlet layer, auth/ACL/permissions, attachment handling, JSP controllers/templates, tags, search, plugins and htmltowiki. Strongest source-evidenced issue: the CSRF protection added in the immediately preceding commits (ChangeLog 2.11.3-git-09/10/11) guards only POST, while several handlers execute privileged state changes on GET; sibling JSPs received explicit guards but page-management/workflow JSPs did not. Several other leads were rejected (htmltowiki XXE hardening gap, AttachmentServlet redirect-validation bypass, users AJAX endpoint, unescaped group-name EL).
